explanation: An apostle who received a direct commission from Jesus Christ to preach the gospel to the Gentiles, independent of the Jewish apostles.
The good news of salvation through faith in the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ, not by works of the law.
The religious regulations and commandments given to Israel through Moses, which according to Paul cannot justify a person before God.
The state in which a person is regarded as innocent or righteous in God's sight solely through faith in Christ, not by their own efforts.
People outside the Jewish nation who, according to Galatians 2, have equal access to salvation as Jews without needing circumcision or following Mosaic law.
The physical ritual act in Jewish tradition that some demanded Gentile Christians undergo to become full members of the faith, which Paul rejects as unnecessary for salvation.
A term for false teachers or Judaizing Christians who infiltrated the church and tried to force Gentiles to follow Jewish customs.
The spiritual liberation from the demands and judgment of the law, which Christ has given to believers through his sacrificial death.
